title: Fakeeh Health hosts international medical experts in Dubai to advance precision surgery

contentHtml:
UAE – Fakeeh Health has opened its fifth annual international conference in Dubai, bringing together surgeons, medical specialists, and healthcare professionals to examine how artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and precision surgery are transforming clinical practice and patient care.

The two-day event, running from November 20 to 21 at JW Marriott Marquis Dubai, is organized in collaboration with MedCore Global Conferences under the theme Innovation, Excellence & Precision in Surgery.

It provides a platform for scientific exchange, professional development and international collaboration on emerging approaches to surgical care.

The conference comes as healthcare providers increasingly adopt AI-powered tools, robotic-assisted procedures and minimally invasive techniques to improve diagnosis, surgical planning and patient recovery.

However, integrating these technologies into clinical practice requires investment in infrastructure, workforce training and safeguards to maintain patient safety and clinical effectiveness.

AI and robotics reshape surgical practice

Dr Mohaymen Abdelghany, Group CEO and Board Member of Fakeeh Health UAE and CEO of Fakeeh University Hospital, said advances in AI and robotics were changing how medical professionals approached diagnosis, surgical planning and complex procedures.

He noted that healthcare providers needed to focus not only on acquiring advanced technologies but also on integrating them effectively into clinical workflows to achieve measurable improvements in patient outcomes.

Dr Abdelghany also highlighted Dubai’s ambition to strengthen its position as a healthcare destination, noting that medical institutions had a role in supporting this agenda through scientific collaboration, continuous professional education and responsible innovation.

The conference’s scientific programme covers several surgical specialties, including neurosurgery, orthopaedics, oncology, transplantation and reconstructive surgery.

Sessions are examining how technological advances can improve the management of complex conditions and support more precise interventions.

AI is a central theme, with experts discussing its applications in medical imaging, surgical planning, clinical decision support and personalised treatment.

These technologies can help clinicians analyse complex medical information and inform treatment decisions, although their adoption must remain guided by clinical evidence and professional judgement.

Robotic-assisted surgery is another key area of discussion.

Participants are exploring how robotic systems can support minimally invasive procedures, improve surgical control and enhance precision during technically demanding operations.

Workforce training and international collaboration

Beyond technology, the conference is addressing the need to prepare healthcare professionals for changes in surgical practice.

Discussions are focusing on specialist training, multidisciplinary teamwork and the importance of ensuring that technology complements rather than replaces clinical expertise.

The event also brings together international specialists and UAE healthcare professionals to share clinical experiences, examine emerging research and discuss practical challenges associated with introducing advanced technologies into hospitals.

For healthcare providers, these discussions have implications for capital investment, clinical governance and workforce development.

Hospitals adopting robotic systems and AI solutions must also consider staff competencies, technology integration and the evidence needed to demonstrate improvements in safety and treatment outcomes.

Fakeeh Health said the conference forms part of its efforts to advance medical education, strengthen professional collaboration and support clinical excellence.

The programme continues on November 21 at JW Marriott Marquis Dubai, with additional scientific sessions examining developments in surgical techniques, AI and robotic technologies.
